legislative_chain.subject: ESTABLISHING the City of Sidney City-Wide Community Reinvestment Area under R.C. 3735.65-.70, designating a Housing Officer and creating a Housing Council
legislative_chain.note: ⚠️ THIS, NOT RES. 69-25, IS THE DESIGNATING ACT — and the register said otherwise until #1998 read both instruments directly. §4 as adopted here tops out at FIFTEEN years / 100% for new commercial and industrial construction; there is no thirty-year tier and no reference to R.C. 122.17 anywhere in it.

legislative_chain.subject: EXPANDING the City-Wide CRA to be coterminous with the City, and amending Res. 84-22 §4 to add a thirty-year megaproject exemption tier

creates_the_thirty_year_tier.verbatim: (e) Up to thirty (30) years, and up to one hundred percent (100%) if the commercial or industrial structure is situated on the site of a megaproject and is owned and occupied by a megaproject operator (as such terms are defined in Ohio Revised Code Section 122.17(A)(12)) …
creates_the_thirty_year_tier.why_it_matters: The 30-year / 100% exemption in the CRA Agreement below rests on this clause, and the clause did not exist until this resolution added it — seven weeks before Res. 80-25 authorized the agreement. [verified] as a SEQUENCE from two instruments and the minutes of both meetings. [open] as a motive: 69-25 names no project, no company and no parcel, and its stated reason is the recent annexations.
creates_the_thirty_year_tier.monitoring_fee: [verified] §5, as amended: 1% of the incentives, minimum $500, MAXIMUM $2,500 a year.

legislative_chain.note: ⚠️ CORRECTED at #1998. The register carried this as the DESIGNATING legislation, reasoning from the CRA Agreement's and Res. 82-25's recitals. Read directly, it amends and expands Res. 84-22. Both readings of the corpus before this one were wrong in the same direction — "Resolution 18-25 … October 2025" (the pre-#1380 register), then "the designating legislation is Res. 69-25" (#1380) — and each was corrected only by reading one document closer to the source. The `-06A` suffix on the area number was the standing clue.

public_records_clause.summary: Before disclosing anything it treats as the Company's "Confidential Information" in response to a public-records request, the City must give the Company written notice and a copy of the request, and allow the Company at least five business days to either negotiate a response with the requester or "pursue, at its sole cost and expense, legal remedies to stop the City's release of the requested information."
public_records_clause.note: The materially identical clause appears at §8.17 of the Development Agreement (Res. 27-26), which additionally binds the City to continuing compliance with the 2023 NDA. Neither clause enlarges any exemption in R.C. 149.43 — both are contractual notice-and-delay obligations layered on top of the statute. See `records_posture`.

distribution.shape: The City takes the $4,000,000 Initial Payment up front and 100% of it. Years 1-3 run $2,500,000 City / $833,333.33 schools. Years 4-11 run level at $1,666,666.67 each. Year 12 is the hinge and the two columns part: the City drops to $166,666.64 while the schools stay at $1,666,666.67. Years 13-15 the City takes $0 and the schools take $2,500,000. Each column sums to $25,000,000; the fifteen annual rows (excluding the up-front payment) sum to the $46,000,000 the CRA Agreement caps PILOTs at — over fifteen rows here against that agreement's fourteen, which is the discrepancy recorded below.

development_agreement_with_school_boards.consents_and_waivers: [verified] §3.1 — in consideration of the agreement, SCSD and UVCC each IRREVOCABLY (a) approve every exemption grantable under the CRA Agreement, (b) waive the notice requirements of R.C. 3735.671, 5709.83 and 5715.27, (c) waive any right to grant approvals required by R.C. 3735.671, and (d) waive any defects or irregularities in the authorization. The boards contracted away their statutory objection rights for the term.
development_agreement_with_school_boards.entirety_of_compensation: [verified] §4.2 — this agreement and the Income Tax Sharing Agreement "provide for the entirety of the compensation to which the City, the School District, and Upper Valley may be entitled" for the exemption.
development_agreement_with_school_boards.term: the duration of the CRA Agreement

income_tax_sharing_agreement.tax_base: the City's permanent 1.5% income tax levy, withheld under Codified Ordinances §142.06 from New Employees
income_tax_sharing_agreement.new_employee_definition: [verified] §1 — an employee first employed at the Project site who has not been subject to the City income tax on income from the Employer, its subsidiaries, affiliates or contractors within the previous two years, and who does not replace a non-new employee.

formula.step_1: the City annually calculates 75% of income tax revenues from all New Employees
formula.step_2: the City annually calculates the real property taxes foregone because of the exemption
formula.scsd_payment: the LESSER of step 1 and (step 2 x 85%)
formula.disbursed: the second week of May each year

income_tax_sharing_agreement.ceiling_intent: [verified] §3 — the districts are to receive "no more than the amount of property tax revenues the Project investment would have generated". The agreement is drafted as partial compensation with a hard ceiling, not as a share of upside.
income_tax_sharing_agreement.reconciliation_note: [inference] The two instruments use different school splits for different money: 84.882116 / 15.117884 for the PILOT distribution (Res. 81-25 Exhibit A) and a flat 85 / 15 for the income-tax sharing (Res. 82-25 §4.3). Not contradictory — different bases — but they are not the same ratio and should not be quoted interchangeably.

schedule_term_discrepancy.finding: [verified] The CRA Agreement's PILOT schedule (Exhibit E) runs FOURTEEN years and totals $46,000,000. The distribution schedule attached to Res. 81-25 (Exhibit A) lays the same $46,000,000 across FIFTEEN years, and its own workspace cells carry "Total $50,000,000 / Per Year $3,333,333.33" — i.e. it was modelled as $50M over 15 years, then reconciled to the columns by tapering Year 12 and zeroing the City in Years 13-15.
schedule_term_discrepancy.why_it_matters: The binding cap is the CRA Agreement's: no more than $46,000,000 of PILOTs, over a 14-year term measured from the first exemption year. The distribution schedule's fifteenth row has no PILOT behind it in the CRA Agreement. Which document governs the final year has not been resolved from the record and is not resolved here.

term.aws_termination: at any time on 90 days' written notice

impact_fees.principle: AWS pays the ordinary metered rate for what it uses AND a monthly reserve-capacity impact fee on the UNUSED portion of its reservation, priced at the reserved fraction of the standard rate. The stated rationale is the cost of maintaining held-back capacity, the lost revenue when usage falls below the reservation, and the lost opportunity to sell that capacity to another customer.
impact_fees.reopener: every three years from the third anniversary of build-out completion, proportionate to actual burden and to any City capacity upgrades

water_and_wastewater_service_agreement.rate_class_covenant: [verified] §2.1 — "During the Term of this Agreement, Provider shall not take steps to create a separate class of water or sewer rates for data centers or similar high level, but highly variable, users of water and sewer services." For ten years the City has contracted away its ability to put this customer, or any customer like it, into its own municipal rate class. Note the contrast with the electric side of the same campus, where AES Ohio's PUCO stipulation of 2026-07-21 is reported to CREATE a data-center tariff.
water_and_wastewater_service_agreement.substitute_supply_right: [verified] §1.5 — if the City for any reason does not supply sufficient water or sewer service, AWS "may secure its own substitute services", and the City must on request provide access to its infrastructure to obtain them. The City's FAQ statement that "no onsite wells will be used" is a present-tense description, not a contractual bar.
water_and_wastewater_service_agreement.regulatory_passthrough: [verified] §6.2 — fines, damages or penalties assessed by a regulator against the City that directly result from AWS consuming or discharging above the §1.2 maxima are direct damages reimbursable by AWS on a pass-through basis.

derived.claim: The cooling loop runs at roughly four cycles of concentration.
derived.basis: Projected makeup 4,600,000 gal/yr divided by projected blowdown 1,160,000 gal/yr (both [verified], §1.1.1 and §1.1.4). A makeup-to-blowdown ratio near 4 is the signature of a closed-loop evaporative cooling tower, and the City's own presentation names "cooling tower discharges" in terms. This is the first documentary handle on this campus's cooling design, which the profile still carries as UNKNOWN.

derived.claim: Projected consumptive loss is 3,440,000 gallons per year, not 4,600,000.
derived.basis: Makeup 4,600,000 minus discharge 1,160,000. The register described the 4,600,000 figure as "projected cooling-water consumption"; the agreement calls it the annual cooling water VOLUME, i.e. the withdrawal, and books the return separately. Consumption is the difference. In cfs: 0.0146, against the cited regulatory Great Miami 7Q10 of 24.0 cfs that is 0.061% — not the 0.08% the register carried.

derived.claim: The reservation takes about a quarter of the City's remaining water headroom.
derived.basis: 1.0 MGD of the ~3.9 MGD the City states as remaining treatment capacity.

derived.claim: The reservation takes about a sixth of the City's remaining sewer headroom.
derived.basis: 0.390493 MGD of the ~2.4 MGD the City states as remaining treatment capacity.

establishment.housing_survey: [verified] The R.C. 3735.66 survey of housing is recited as "on file at the City Hall, 201 West Poplar Street" and is NOT attached to the resolution. [open] — not in corpus.

exemption_ceiling_as_adopted.commercial_industrial_new_construction: (d) Up to fifteen (15) years, and up to one hundred percent (100%) for the construction of new commercial (including residential with more than two units) and industrial structures, the term and percentage of which shall be negotiated on a case-by-case basis in advance of construction occurring.
exemption_ceiling_as_adopted.no_megaproject_clause: [verified] §4 as adopted runs (a) through (d) and ends there. There is no clause (e), no thirty-year tier, and no reference to R.C. 122.17 anywhere in this instrument. The thirty-year megaproject tier was added by Res. 69-25 on 2025-09-08 — seven weeks before Res. 80-25 authorized a 30-year / 100% CRA Agreement with Amazon Data Services.
exemption_ceiling_as_adopted.dwelling_extension: [verified] A DWELLING's exemption may be extended up to ten additional years for a certified historic structure — the only path past fifteen years in the resolution as adopted, and it does not reach commercial or industrial property.

It is a live body: the 2025-10-27 minutes record that "the CRA Housing Council met on October 23, 2025, and unanimously resolved to recommend that City Council approve" the Amazon CRA agreement, and the City's 2026 resolution index carries appointments to it (Res. 37-26, 38-26, 74-25). fields.instrument: City of Sidney Resolution No. 69-25 — authorizing the expansion of the City's Sidney City-Wide Community Reinvestment Area and amending Resolution 84-22, passed 2025-09-08
fields.body: Council of the City of Sidney, Ohio
fields.title_verbatim: A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE EXPANSION OF THE CITY'S SIDNEY CITY-WIDE COMMUNITY REINVESTMENT AREA AND AMENDING RESOLUTION 84-22

amends.what_it_did: Created and established the Sidney City-Wide Community Reinvestment Area, assigned designation #149-72424-06 by the Director of the Ohio Department of Development.

expansion.verbatim: SECTION 2. Pursuant to Section 3735.66 of the CRA Act, the City-Wide CRA is hereby amended and expanded to include the Expanded Area.
expansion.effect: [verified] The expansion is stated in §1 to leave the City-Wide CRA "having boundaries which are currently coterminous with the City". The Expanded Area is described and depicted on the instrument's Exhibit A (pp. 7-18), which is image-only and NOT read here.
expansion.what_the_minutes_add: [verified] Community Development Director Barbara Dulworth told Council the expansion "would extend the city Community Reinvestment Area (CRA) boundaries to incorporate the recent annexations, including the 243.092 acres on the north side of Millcreek Road, west of Vandemark Road and the 53.16 acres of land west of Vandemark Road, south of Fair Road." Source: data/documents/sidney/council/City Council Minutes September 08, 2025.pdf p. 2.
expansion.note: [inference] "The north side of Millcreek Road, west of Vandemark Road" is the same locator the Res. 80-25 recitals use for the Amazon Data Services project site. The minutes do not join the two, and this resolution names no project; recorded as a locator match, not a finding.

megaproject_tier.verbatim: (e) Up to thirty (30) years, and up to one hundred percent (100%) if the commercial or industrial structure is situated on the site of a megaproject and is owned and occupied by a megaproject operator (as such terms are defined in Ohio Revised Code Section 122.17(A)(12)), or is not situated on the site of a megaproject but is owned and occupied by a megaproject supplier that meets the requirements described in Ohio Revised Code Section 122.17(A)(13)(b)
megaproject_tier.ceiling_before_this_resolution: [verified] Res. 84-22 §4 as adopted ran (a) through (d) and stopped at FIFTEEN years / 100% for new commercial and industrial construction. It contains no thirty-year tier and no reference to R.C. 122.17.
megaproject_tier.thresholds_as_stated_to_council: [verified] "large-scale development project meeting specific investment or payroll thresholds, such as at least $1 billion in capital investment or creating $75 million in annual payroll. She noted that the Ohio Department of Development (ODOD) was responsible for certifying megaprojects." — the minutes of this meeting, p. 2. These are STAFF'S characterisation of R.C. 122.17(A)(12); the statute itself is not quoted in the instrument.
megaproject_tier.downstream: [verified] Res. 80-25 (2025-10-27) authorized a CRA Agreement whose exemption is 30 years at 100%. [verified] The minutes of THAT meeting recite this resolution as the authority: "Per the Ohio Revised Code, and the recently adopted revised Sidney City-Wide CRA, property tax abatements for up to 30 years can be approved for megaprojects or megaproject operators."
megaproject_tier.what_is_still_open: [open] Whether the Ohio Department of Development has in fact DESIGNATED this campus a megaproject. The 2025-10-27 minutes say only that the project "meets the requirements to be designated" — eligibility asserted by staff, in the present tense, not a designation stated as made. No ODOD certification is in the corpus.

monitoring_fee.verbatim: SECTION 5. An annual monitoring fee to the City of Sidney of one percent (1%) of the amount of the incentives, or a minimum of Five Hundred Dollars ($500.00), up to a maximum of Twenty-five Hundred Dollars ($2,500.00) annually is required for commercial and industrial projects.
monitoring_fee.note: [verified] The fee is 1% of the incentives but CAPPED AT $2,500 a year. Recorded because the cap is a fact about the instrument, not an argument: it is what the City charges to administer an exemption of any size, including a thirty-year one.

other_sections: [verified] §3 — all residential, commercial and industrial properties in the Expanded Area, consistent with applicable zoning, are eligible.
[verified] §6 — "Except as amended hereby, Resolution 84-22 shall remain in full force and effect."
[verified] §7 — a copy of the Resolution goes to the Shelby County Auditor, sent by the Community Development Director.
[verified] §8 — the Community Development Director is authorized to petition the ODOD Director for approval of the expanded City-Wide CRA under R.C. 3735.66.

vote.verbatim: Councilmember Roddy made a motion to adopt Resolution No. 69-25 as presented; seconded by Councilmember VanMatre. Upon a roll call vote, the motion passed unanimously. Resolution No. 69-25 is hereby adopted.
vote.note: [verified] A roll call WAS taken; the minutes record its outcome and not its individual votes. That is the form of these minutes for an uncontested item — contrast Res. 82-25 on 2025-10-27, where the same clerk journalled seven names because the vote was divided.
vote.deliberation: [verified] "There were no questions or comments on this topic." Recorded verbatim because it is the whole of the public deliberation on the clause that created the thirty-year tier.

what_this_instrument_does_not_establish: IT NAMES NO PROJECT, NO COMPANY AND NO PARCEL. Every word about Amazon, the campus or the data center in this file comes from the MINUTES or from a later instrument, and is labelled as such. A reader must not cite this resolution for the campus.

THE EXPANDED AREA IS NOT READ. Exhibit A (pp. 7-18) is the boundary map and legal description, and it is image-only. The two annexation acreages above are the minutes' account of it, not a reading of the exhibit. [open]
IT GRANTS NOTHING. §4 sets ceilings to be "negotiated on a case-by-case basis in advance of construction"; the grant is the CRA Agreement, authorized separately by Res. 80-25.
